title: 2025-12-04-redwood-discovery-model-selection-evora-payments
header:
Date: 2025-12-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (CTO, Evora), Maya Lopez (Head of ML), Samir Patel (Infra Lead)
summary: Initial discovery focused on model selection for payments-related NLU and document parsing workloads. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments due to PII/regulatory constraints; primary concerns are context length for multi-doc reconciliation, multilingual support (EN/ES/PT), tool-calling (payment APIs and internal toolchain), latency vs cost, and security (VPC, KMS, audit logs). Agreed to follow up with a technical deep dive and pilot benchmark on a 32k and 128k context model. Redwood to share pricing and SOC2/security docs.
topics: Model options: open models and tradeoffs (LLaMA variants, Mistral-like, redwood-verified profiles)
Context length needs: 8k vs 32k vs 128k and tokenization implications for receipts/invoices
Multilingual: Spanish/Portuguese handling and fine-tuning vs prompts
Tool-calling: safe connector patterns for payment APIs, function calling vs tooling integration
Deployment modes: Hosted API (fast), Dedicated (reserved GPU), Private (VPC/on-prem) and compliance tradeoffs
Security: SOC 2, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, data residency
action_items: Alex Morgan - Send Evora pricing sheet and example Dedicated pricing (due: 2025-12-08)
Priya Shah - Schedule technical deep dive/demo with infra team and bring benchmarks template (due: 2025-12-10)
Maya Lopez - Prepare a sample prompt set and example documents for pilot (due: 2025-12-09)
Samir Patel - Share current infra diagram and compliance checklist for VPC/on-prem discussion (due: 2025-12-11)
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 and security whitepaper link
Schedule 90-minute technical deep dive (AE/SE + Evora infra + ML) next week
Run a pilot: 2-week benchmark comparing 32k and 128k model variants on Evora sample dataset (focus: latency, token cost, correctness)
Provide Dedicated capacity options and timeline for Private deployment (rough estimate)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE, and with me is Priya our SE. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Daniel Kim: Hi this is Daniel, CTO at Evora.
[00:11] Maya Lopez: Maya here, head of ML.
[00:13] Samir Patel: Samir, infra.
[00:15] Priya Shah: Great, thanks. The agenda is model selection, context needs, multilingual, tool-calling and deployment options. Does that work?
[00:24] Daniel Kim: Yep, that's perfect. High-level, we process merchant disputes and receipts, lots of scanned PDFs and chat transcripts, we need good multi-doc reasoning and sometimes 3-4 page context. Also some Spanish and Portuguese.
[00:36] Alex Morgan: Got it. Are you currently using any LLM provider in prod?
[00:40] Maya Lopez: We're proof-of-concepting with a hosted provider, but costs are getting high and we hit rate limits. Also redacted logs are a pain for compliance.
[00:49] Samir Patel: And we have strict requirements around PII — PCI-adjacent stuff — so VPC and KMS are on the table.
[00:56] Priya Shah: Makes sense. For model selection, are you leaning open models or closed like Anthropic/OpenAI?
[01:02] Daniel Kim: We'd prefer open models if the perf is there; also fine-tuning may be needed. But we care about latency and cost.
[01:09] Alex Morgan: So typical tradeoff. With Redwood Hosted you can start fast, we expose curated open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles. Dedicated gives reserved GPUs and predictable throughput, Private gives a customer-managed control plane with VPC and on-prem.
[01:23] Maya Lopez: For context lengths — we have examples that exceed 50k tokens when you include multiple invoices and chat logs. How do you handle that?
[01:31] Priya Shah: Good question. We support models with 8k, 32k, and 128k context lengths depending on the model. There's also a KV cache / prefix caching strategy to handle repeated prefixes which reduces cost and latency for long sessions. (Note: sometimes transcribed as KV cash in our export)
[01:46] Daniel Kim: What's the quality delta between 32k and 128k?
[01:50] Priya Shah: In many tasks, 32k is sufficient, but when you need cross-document reasoning across many pages there's measurable improvement with 128k. The tradeoff is memory and per-token cost — on Dedicated you can pick a quantized variant to lower cost.
[02:05] Samir Patel: And what about multilingual? Spanish/Portuguese — do models need fine-tuning or do base models handle it?
[02:12] Priya Shah: Some base open models are multilingual out of the box, but for domain-specific terms (payments, merchant names) a small fine-tune or retrieval-augmented prompts help. We also support embeddings that can be language-aware for search.
[02:24] Maya Lopez: Tool-calling: we need the model to call internal payment validation APIs and redact tokens before logging. How does Redwood handle function or tool calling?
[02:33] Alex Morgan: We support structured function/tool calling and streaming. There are recommended safe connector patterns: run a policy layer in your infra to validate calls before executing payment flows. For Private deployments you can keep calls inside your VPC.
[02:47] Daniel Kim: Are there examples of customers doing tool-calling for payments?
[02:50] Priya Shah: Yes, we've seen fintechs use function calling with a middleware that does auth and PII redaction. Redwood's runtime supports function calls and you can route those to a private webhook.
[03:00] Samir Patel: Latency is critical for fraud check flows. What SLOs can you hit on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[03:07] Priya Shah: Hosted is optimized for latency but is multi-tenant; Dedicated gives predictable p99 latency and throughput because you have reserved GPU pools. We publish model latency profiles; for example, a 32k variant on Dedicated can get p95 around X ms for short responses (note: numbers discussed verbally).
[03:22] Alex Morgan: Also caching and batching configuration in Redwood Optimize can reduce unit cost without sacrificing SLOs.
[03:29] Maya Lopez: On security, we need SOC 2 type II, audit logs, KMS integration and SAML SSO.
[03:35] Alex Morgan: Redwood supports SOC 2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations. For Private we can do a customer-managed KMS and full audit log forwarding. We'll send the security whitepaper after the call.
[03:48] Daniel Kim: If we go Private, what's the timeline and effort?
[03:52] Priya Shah: Usually there's a prep phase for networking and IAM, then a deployment window. Timeline depends on on-prem vs VPC; for VPC it's often 4-8 weeks with some back-and-forth. We'll give rough timelines in the follow-up.
[04:04] Maya Lopez: For the pilot, we'd like to compare a 32k and a 128k model on our dataset — measure latency, token cost and correctness on reconciliations.
[04:13] Alex Morgan: Sounds good. We'll provision test endpoints. For Dedicated pilot we can reserve a small pool, or you can test on Hosted first to speed up.
[04:21] Samir Patel: How does billing look for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[04:25] Alex Morgan: Hosted is usage-based (tokens/embeddings). Dedicated is committed capacity with monthly/annual contracts. We'll send the pricing sheet with sample math for your workload.
[04:35] Maya Lopez: Any limitations on model tool-calling with longer contexts?
[04:39] Priya Shah: The runtime handles KV cache and long-context models, but you should design tool call payloads to be concise. For very long chains of reasoning, we sometimes recommend chunking and using retrieval + embeddings.
[04:51] Daniel Kim: Competitors — we're talking to OpenAI and Vertex too. How do you compare?
[04:56] Alex Morgan: Many providers offer similar API simplicity; our differentiators are the production-first runtime, dedicated capacity, Private deployment options and tooling to optimize cost/perf. Also transparent model profiles and recommendations for quantization and batching.
[05:12] Maya Lopez: Any specifics on quantization? We saw some quality regressions in early experiments.
[05:17] Priya Shah: We provide quantization recommendations by workload; some models quantize well with minimal quality loss, others need evals. Redwood Optimize helps automate that. We'll include recommended profiles for the models we propose.
[05:30] Samir Patel: For data residency — we have EU merchants. Can Private handle EU-only data residency?
[05:36] Alex Morgan: Yes, Private with customer-managed control plane can be set up in EU regions to meet residency needs; Hosted also has region options but Private gives more control.
[05:46] Maya Lopez: Ok, let's talk specific model candidates — open models that Redwood curates?
[05:51] Priya Shah: We typically evaluate LLaMA-family variants, community long-context models, and optimized Mistral-like models. For your use case, we'd pick a 32k open model as baseline and a 128k variant for cross-document tasks. If higher throughput is needed, consider a quantized Dedicated variant.
[06:08] Daniel Kim: Can we get a benchmark run with our sample data?
[06:11] Alex Morgan: Yes. Priya will own the benchmark template and we'll provision endpoints.
[06:15] Priya Shah: I'll send the benchmark spreadsheet. Please include sample documents and expected outputs so we can score correctness.
[06:22] Maya Lopez: We'll prepare 200 sample cases and expected reconciliation labels.
[06:26] Daniel Kim: About fine-tuning — is that supported on Hosted?
[06:29] Priya Shah: Hosted supports fine-tuning on some models; Dedicated/Private gives more options for custom models and on-prem fine-tuning. We can discuss tradeoffs — often retrieval augmentation is faster and safer for PII.
[06:41] Alex Morgan: For logging and redaction, we can route logs to your log storage and apply redaction rules before retention.
[06:48] Samir Patel: What about SLA for Dedicated?
[06:51] Alex Morgan: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. We'll include SLA language in the follow-up.
[07:00] Maya Lopez: Any gotchas with tokenization for receipts? We have a lot of small numeric fields that expand into many tokens.
[07:06] Priya Shah: Tokenization varies by tokenizer; we can profile tokenization overhead on your docs as part of the pilot and provide recommendations, like normalizing numbers or pre-parsing structured fields.
[07:18] Daniel Kim: How do we protect credentials when models call our payment API?
[07:22] Priya Shah: Best practice is to have a middleware inside your VPC that receives signed call intents from the model runtime, validates, and then executes the API call with stored secrets — so secrets never go through the model provider.
[07:35] Alex Morgan: Quick recap — Redwood will: share pricing, SOC2/security docs, benchmark template, and propose timeline for Dedicated/Private. Evora will: prepare sample dataset, infra diagram, and internal success criteria for the pilot.
[07:50] Daniel Kim: Sounds good. One last question: how much engineering lift for Private?
[07:55] Priya Shah: Depends; if you choose VPC Private with our control plane, less than full on-prem. If fully on-prem, more lift. We'll detail steps in the follow-up.
[08:06] Maya Lopez: Great. Thanks everyone.
[08:08] Alex Morgan: Thanks, we'll send the docs and schedule the tech deep dive.
[44:30] (end)
